themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters spiked to 18 complaints 2 weeks ago—a 476% increase from the 3.1-per-week baseline (z-score: 9.68)—signaling a sudden public safety or policing perception shift in Bed-Stuy that warrants investigation into what specific incidents or conditions triggered the surge.
evidence: 18 non-emergency police complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average (476% spike)
Z-score of 9.68 indicates extreme statistical significance
No corresponding reporting in local news or Reddit suggests under-covered story
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct leadership and residents about what specific incidents or conditions drove the complaint surge
Cross-reference 311 data with NYPD crime stats and precinct activity logs for the same period

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Complaints Quadruple
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints reached 6 last week—a 500% spike from the 1.0-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.08)—suggesting either a genuine increase in street-level drug activity or a shift in resident reporting behavior in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% spike)
Z-score of 4.08 indicates high statistical significance
Temporal alignment with non-emergency police spike suggests possible broader public safety concern
reporting_angles: Talk to residents and local business owners in hotspot blocks to understand what they're observing and reporting
Interview NYPD and community policing officers about enforcement patterns and whether they've detected increased activity

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Incidents Accelerate
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints hit 8 two weeks ago—a 392% increase from the 1.6-per-week baseline (z-score: 4.26)—indicating a pattern of unauthorized cutting, removal, or damage to street trees that may reflect either contractor activity or environmental degradation.
evidence: 8 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly average (392% spike)
Z-score of 4.26 indicates high statistical significance
Aligns with 500% spike in street sign damage, suggesting possible construction or infrastructure work
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYC Department of Parks or private contractors are conducting work without proper notification or permits
Map the geolocation of complaints to identify whether damage is concentrated in a specific block or development zone

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Lot Conditions Deteriorating
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 20 two weeks ago (186% spike from 7.0 baseline; z-score: 4.11), while lot condition complaints spiked to 6 (1100% spike from 0.5 baseline; z-score: 5.5)—together suggesting either a sanitation/maintenance gap or deteriorating conditions on vacant or under-managed properties in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 20 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.0 weekly average (186% spike)
6 lot condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% spike)
Combined z-scores (4.11 and 5.5) indicate highly anomalous deterioration in physical disorder
reporting_angles: Identify the specific blocks or properties where lot conditions are worst; interview neighbors and property owners about neglect
Investigate whether graffiti is linked to gang activity, or whether it reflects a backlog in NYPD or community response

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints tripled to 3 two weeks ago (500% spike from 0.5 baseline; z-score: 5.0), potentially indicating accidental or intentional damage from heavy vehicle traffic, construction, or public disorder that may signal broader street maintenance concerns.
evidence: 3 street sign damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike)
Z-score of 5.0 indicates high statistical significance
Temporal alignment with illegal tree damage spike suggests possible coordinated construction or infrastructure work
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with Department of Transportation and Parks work orders to determine if city-sponsored projects are ongoing
Survey a sample of blocks to assess condition of street signage and identify patterns in damage
